correctness.rationale: The omitted-set history is hit by precisely the uncollected target sets: a transversal of size at most s can be padded to size s. With a fresh label on each slot replacement, transversals are interval covers. The minimum interval cover greedily uses the interval ending farthest right at the first uncovered time (any first interval in an optimum can be exchanged for it). At an epoch boundary the k current intervals end just before the next uses of their respective slots, so the farthest endpoint is just before the next complete coupon epoch. The next interval is selected at this boundary, not necessarily born there. The ideal completion time is exactly the end of epoch s and the iid slot word regenerates there. Mapping formal labels to finite labels only identifies labels, which cannot increase the transversal number. Condition on the whole slot word and use independent draw randomizers for labels: given no earlier recurrence, update j has at most j-1 previously seen eligible labels out of n-k. The slot indices need not be independent of the realized label identities. The conditional union bound up to the slot-measurable T* gives the stated error, and injectivity through T* implies equality. The geometric decomposition gives the PGF, E T*=skHk and Var(T*)=s(k^2 Hk^(2)-kHk), verifying the second factorial moment. For fixed k,s and n-k>=2sk, each fresh prescribed sk-step block succeeds conditionally with probability at least (2k)^(-sk), uniformly over histories. This bounds the expected residual time on the discrepancy event at T* and yields the O(1/n) mean error rather than inferring it from TV convergence alone. For growing k the stated hypothesis makes the coupling error o(1), and independent collector limits give the s-fold Gumbel sum.
residual_risks: The bounded replay checks a small finite-population shadow, not the uniform bound or limit; those follow from the proof. The expectation estimate is only for fixed k,s.

value.rationale: The near-census regime is a natural opposite end of the Markovian super-coupon model. The epoch identity explains why the limiting law differs from the standard single-Gumbel law for s>=2 and why changing the goal size changes the number of independent epochs. It also gives the explicit finite error control and mean estimate, rather than only an asymptotic law or an isolated low-parameter example.
residual_risks: Neither the fixed observed-size conjecture nor a uniform mean estimate in the growing-k regime is settled.
